details: Line of Sight: Straight line drawn from observer's eye to target point.
Angle of Elevation: Angle between line of sight and horizontal baseline when looking UP.
Angle of Depression: Angle between line of sight and horizontal baseline when looking DOWN.
Angle of depression equals angle of elevation from observer object due to alternate interior angles.
evidence_or_examples: Pole 6 m high casts shadow 2√3 m => tan θ = 6/(2√3) = √3 => θ = 60°.
Circus artist climbing 20 m rope tied to pole top at 30° => sin 30° = AB/20 => pole height = 10 m.

details: Set up coupled right-angled triangles to compute unknown heights or distance between objects.
evidence_or_examples: Lighthouse height 75 m, ship depression angles 30° and 45°: ship distances 75 m and 75√3 m => ship distance = 75(√3 - 1) m ≈ 54.9 m.
Statue 1.6 m on pedestal, top angles 60° and 45° => pedestal height h = 0.8(√3 + 1) m.
